text:
aria: Heads-up — noticing a 95th-percentile host-side latency jump on streaming requests since yesterday's runtime change. Spike happens during parse/tokenize phase under concurrency >120.

mike: saw that in dashboards, /ingress/preparse host CPU climbs and stays hot. traces attached? :thinking_face:

aria: attaching pprof and tiny flame (large attached off-thread). quick snippet below:
```
(pprof) top
3.2s 30.5% runtime.parseToken
1.8s 17.1% net.http2.parseFrame
0.9s 8.6% kvcache.lookup
0.7s 6.6% grpc.streamSlice
0.5s 4.7% runtime.alloc
```

aria: Also noticing KV cache miss rate up ~2x for these streams, which increases hostside tail (more parse + fallback path).

jamie: any recent kernel-selection or batching heuristic changes landed? could be a small rebuild switched to conservative kernels so parse path is slower.

sasha: I pushed a tiny change to batching heuristics last week (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1789) — it preferred larger batch sizes for low-latency tiers. Might affect bufferization/parse interleaving.

olivia: can we repro locally with a synthetic client that drives concurrent streaming with small chunks? I can run a repeatable harness.

mike: yes pls. run against canary. command we use:
```
./tools/harness --mode streaming --concurrency 150 --chunk-ms 12 --duration 120 --target canary-host:8080
```

aria: ran that for 2m. repro is stable. I diffed preparse traces: more writes into small buffers (lots of smallwrite syscalls) which causes http2 hpack path to stall -> parseFrame cost rises.

jamie: smallwrite pattern -> writev coalescing gone? last flush optimization in syscall shim was reverted in 2024-02-01 build maybe.

sasha: right — revert was in the shim to fix a rare ordering flake. I can try reintroducing writev coalesce gated behind a flag.

mike: before changing IO behavior, can we mitigate at tokenization level? aria, what's the tokenize hotpath like? maybe switch to streaming lexer that avoids alloc per fragment.

aria: current tokenization allocs ~0.5 allocs/op when fragments are <64B. Streaming lexer reduces that to ~0.05 allocs/op in my microbench.

olivia: patch idea: add a fast-path in preparse that if payload len < 128 and headers stable, use in-place lexer + zero-copy buffer reference. minimal risk.

sre-bot: Incident ticket IN-2024-042 created for host-preparse-latency. Assigned to eng-runtime.

mike: good. also roll a KV cache instrumentation to see exact miss cause — could be eviction thrash from larger batches reducing per-key locality.

aria: added extra kv tagging in canary, sample output:
```
kv.metrics: requests=23k hits=18k misses=5k miss_rate=0.217 eviction_rate=0.03
hot_shard=13 hit_rate=0.60
```

aria: miss_rate spike aligns with peak concurrency windows.

jamie: that hints batching changed request coalescing on ingress -> more distinct prefixes per batch -> worse KV locality. sasha's batching change likely the root.

sasha: I'll roll a small tweak: prefer per-connection micro-batches when streaming (keep batch size cap at 8 for streaming paths). Will push as a canary flag.

mike: let's test three axes in canary: (1) writev coalesce re-enable, (2) streaming-lexer fast-path, (3) batching cap for streams. each in isolation then combined.

olivia: I'll run the harness and capture pprof + kv metrics. timeline:
- 1749803000 run baseline canary
- 1749803600 run canary+lexer
- 1749804200 run canary+batchcap
- 1749804567 run combined

aria: quick results summary:
- baseline: 95p latency 210ms, parseToken 30%
- +lexer: 95p 160ms, parseToken down to 18%, allocs/op reduced
- +batchcap: 95p 175ms, kv miss_rate down to 0.12
- combined: 95p 120ms, kv miss_rate 0.09, parseToken 12%

jamie: that's promising. any regression in throughput? we saw a small drop (~3%) in max qps for combined, but tail improvements worth it.

mike: let's open a follow-up PR that wires these as feature flags defaulted for streaming routes, include tests and perf numbers. ref: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1833

sasha: I'll prepare the canary rollout plan. deploy-bot, start canary when PR merged.

deploy-bot: Started canary deploy runtime-canary id=canary-20240210 targeting eng-runtime (3 nodes)

olivia: will monitor. If no regression in 2 hours, promote and schedule cut for next patch.

aria: thanks all. follow-ups: add kv trace sampling for 1% of requests and add unit tests for lexer fast-path.

mike: nice triage. record this in postmortem notes if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
